I had a girlfriend who tried to control everything once. It was a terrible experience and ended poorly. I realized at the end of that relationship that in order for a relationship to succeed, the respect needs to be mutual, at least like 90% of the time. (there's give and take with everything).

The toughest thing about lack of respect from a partner, is that the effects on self-esteem can be devastating. One may wonder how it is that they can do so much and receive so little. This turns into resentment towards your partner and when it hits that point, there's no amount of fixing it that will suffice. It will end poorly.

There's really only two things that can set things right.

First option - you can try to brute force your way back into being a 'partner' in the relationship instead of a subservient. This will require a lot of willpower and energy in the terms of standing your ground. You need to have some wins in the relationship. IE: "Hey, in order for this to work, we need to move in together, I need to experience living with you before I marry you, and if I can't have that, it's not going to work out in the long term for me".

Second option - end the relationship, and start a new relationship later when you find a partner that respects you. I know this option may seem harsh, or even tough, but the truth is, it'll suck for about 3 months, then you'll get over it. Invite buddies over to hang all the time, don't give into your ex and just grow into finding yourself again so that another amazing person can share who that is together, 50-50 with you.

Good luck.
